notes:
Background: Luma Platforms builds an in-app conversational and search experience for mid-market SaaS customers (support + knowledge discovery). Started with Redwood Hosted API for quick integration (chat + embeddings). After initial success, team wants Dedicated POC to guarantee throughput and reduce per-token costs for production rollout.

Key contacts: CTO - Arjun Patel (technical lead), Product PM - Erin Walsh (owns use-case), AE - Maya Chen, SE - Diego Alvarez.

Conversation summary: demo 2026-02-10 (hosted API) -> satisfied with latency & output quality. Pricing discussion 2026-02-17. Luma requested a Dedicated POC to validate cost/perf at scale and to test canary + automated fallback routing for availability.

POC goals (quantitative): p50 latency target < 120ms (chat), p95 < 400ms; steady-state throughput ~30 req/s (500-800 token context); cost target: reduce hosted marginal token cost by ~40% using Dedicated + quantized variants. Functional parity: responses must match hosted baseline on 95% of eval prompts.

POC scope: 2-week Dedicated POC. Environment: VPC peered Dedicated pool in us-east-1, with failover region us-west-2. Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over monitored windows (30m / 2h). Fallback routing: prefer primary model variant (redwood-chat-13b) -> fallback to quantized variant (redwood-chat-13b-q4) on high latency/cost; region failover to us-west-2 if capacity or AZ issues. Rollback triggers: error rate > 1% above baseline, p95 latency > 2x baseline, automated eval quality degradation > 5% on sentinel prompts.

Model variants considered: redwood-chat-13b (fp16), redwood-chat-13b-q4_0 (quantized), redwood-instruct-7b (backup low-cost), embeddings: redwood-embed-2k. Routing policy ideas: latency-first for key customer routes, cost-aware for batch reranking jobs.

Telemetry & observability: need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, custom tracing hooks for QA, and access to rollup logs in S3 (audit requirement). Luma asked for demo of Redwood Console dashboards and alerting during canary windows.

Security/compliance notes: SSO via SAML required; must support KMS for key wrapping and provide audit logging retention 1 year. Data residency: customer data stored in us-east-1 for this POC. Legal requested Redwood security FAQ and DPA redline (drive links above).

Procurement flow: Procurement expects final pricing + Dedicated commit options. Estimated ARR moved from internal $30k to negotiation at $50-120k depending on committed capacity. Procurement signoff is current blocker (finance meeting week of 2026-03-15).

Recent timeline (high level):
- 2026-01-15: Intro call, initial fit confirmed.
- 2026-02-10: Hosted API demo + rapid prototype integrated into staging.
- 2026-02-17: Pricing & capacity conversation; Luma requests Dedicated POC.
- 2026-02-18: Deep technical call (SE) - network & KMS requirements (fireflies id ff_2026-02-18_xYz12).
- 2026-02-25: Security questionnaire submitted; Redwood provided SOC2 docs.
- 2026-03-05: Final POC scope agreed; next step is kickoff and provisioning.

Quotes / call snippets: "We saw immediate improvement on smaller workloads with Hosted — Dedicated is about economics and SLAs for production." — Arjun (CTO).

Next steps (detailed):
1) Redwood SE to provision Dedicated pool (us-east-1) and share endpoint + sample creds (target 2026-03-10).
2) Luma to upload test dataset + baseline eval prompts to shared drive (by 2026-03-09).
3) Sync on canary rollout plan with monitoring/alert thresholds (schedule 60m working session).
4) Legal + Procurement follow up: DPA redline and committed capacity options.

POC acceptance criteria (short): latency & throughput SLOs met, cost reduction validated, no security compliance gaps, successful canary to 100% without rollback within evaluation period.
